overview: The Medford School Committee is the governing body for Medford Public Schools, responsible for district policy, operating budgets, superintendent evaluation and hiring, and facility planning. Across meetings recorded from October 2019 through October 2026, the committee addressed remote learning during the COVID-19 pandemic, extensive collective bargaining, district safety reviews, and systemic infrastructure challenges. The committee led major long-term capital undertakings, including submitting Statements of Interest to the Massachusetts School Building Authority and advancing design options for a comprehensive high school building project. Following the departure of Superintendent Marice Edouard-Vincent in early 2025, the committee appointed Suzanne Galusi first as interim and then as permanent superintendent. At its most recent meetings, the committee is managing school space and HVAC renovations, elementary reassignment rules, after-school expansion, and district strategic planning.

threads.name: Medford High School building project
threads.summary: The committee initiated planning for high school renovations by creating a flagship vision committee and authorizing a Statement of Interest to the Massachusetts School Building Authority core program in 2022. After an initial submission, the district resubmitted and Medford High School was accepted into the MSBA core program eligibility phase in December 2023. In 2024, the committee established the Medford Comprehensive High School Building Committee, finalized its governance structure, and selected Left Field as Owner's Project Manager. During 2025 and 2026, the committee endorsed a Construction Manager at Risk delivery method, approved the educational plan, adjusted design alternatives to accommodate a 1967 DCR deed restriction on Edgerly Field, and reviewed narrowed schematic alternatives.

threads.name: District superintendent leadership and evaluation
threads.summary: The committee regularly established annual performance goals and completed composite evaluations for Superintendent Marice Edouard-Vincent, granting a four-year contract extension in April 2021. In late 2024, following executive session contract negotiations, Superintendent Edouard-Vincent announced her departure effective January 2025. The committee appointed Assistant Superintendent Suzanne Galusi as interim superintendent and approved her transition plan and conflict disclosures. In February 2026, following annual evaluation feedback, the committee voted to appoint Suzanne Galusi as permanent superintendent, subsequently approving a three-year contract in May 2026.

threads.name: Collective bargaining and labor agreements
threads.summary: The committee conducted recurrent negotiations and approved memoranda of agreement across all district bargaining units, including the Medford Teachers Association, paraprofessionals, administrators, nurses, custodians, and cafeteria staff. Protracted negotiations with the teachers union led to state mediation in autumn 2022 and an initial failed ratification vote before a four-year contract was finalized in December 2022. Successor agreements were negotiated and ratified across subsequent cycles, including a three-year contract with the teachers association in April 2025 and an agreement with the Massachusetts Nurses Association through fiscal year 2028. The committee also resolved contracts for support units, including custodians, cafeteria workers, and paraprofessionals.

threads.name: District facilities and HVAC capital upgrades
threads.summary: Aging building systems prompted repeated facilities interventions, including high school hot water heater replacements and roof leak repairs at McGlynn Elementary. Following severe heating and cooling failures across multiple schools, the committee approved a partial decarbonization HVAC scope and recommended a $25.7 million bond request for major HVAC replacements at McGlynn and Andrews schools. In 2025 and 2026, the committee approved a $22.7 million schematic design for HVAC electrification and roof replacement at Roberts Elementary with MSBA reimbursement and chose a geothermal heat pump system for Missituk Elementary. The committee also adopted a policy restricting replacement fossil-fuel equipment and approved capital allocations for security, water wellness, and intercom systems.

threads.name: School climate, safety, and discipline
threads.summary: Following student protests and violent incidents including a bathroom assault and a December 2022 stabbing at Medford High School, the committee enacted an emergency 10-point safety plan and commissioned consultant Michael Welch to conduct a climate and security review. The committee monitored discipline reforms, requiring regular suspension reports, piloting restorative justice practices, updating bullying intervention policies, and revising the dress code. The committee introduced vape sensors, security camera reporting, and hall-monitoring protocols, while adopting the Panorama survey tool to measure school climate. Updated guidelines for academic honesty, student handbooks, and physical restraint policies were also codified.

threads.name: Curriculum, literacy, and graduation standards
threads.summary: The district expanded early literacy screening pilots and foundational instruction, ultimately adopting Houghton Mifflin Harcourt's 'Into Reading' curriculum in June 2023 following multi-year reviews of evidence-based reading practices. At the secondary level, mathematics pathways were restructured to introduce an integrated mathematics sequence alongside revised acceleration placement rules. Following the passage of statewide Question 2 in November 2024, the committee amended Policy IKF to remove the MCAS competency requirement for graduation, replacing it with local coursework completion benchmarks while maintaining mandated state testing participation. The committee also adopted policies governing the use of generative artificial intelligence in academic settings.

threads.name: Before- and after-school childcare expansion
threads.summary: Elementary before- and after-school programs faced severe staffing shortages and persistent waitlists across multiple school years. The committee implemented incremental tuition increases, revised staff pay, created early pickup options, and established a lottery system for incoming kindergartners to replace static waitlists. In 2025, the committee engaged the Belmont After School Enrichment Collaborative (BASIC) to evaluate operations, leading to an expansion of 150 seats, full-time site coordinators, and restructured rate cards. By autumn 2026, the administration reported a 68 percent reduction in waitlists alongside a 50 percent increase in overall program enrollment.

threads.name: Elementary enrollment and school capacity planning
threads.summary: Imbalances in student enrollment generated severe overcrowding, particularly at Roberts Elementary School, leading staff and parents to request redistricting reviews. To address immediate capacity limits, the committee relocated Medford Early Education Program preschool classrooms from Roberts to Missituk Elementary and funded additional staffing. The committee commissioned an HMFH space utilization study that examined grade reconfigurations, but voted in July 2026 to delay any potential 5–8 middle school grade restructuring until at least 2028. In late 2026, the committee began reviewing a formal policy to regulate and prioritize elementary school reassignment requests.

periods.narrative: The committee concluded business for the term by reviewing elementary literacy pilot screening tools, addressing bus safety concerns, approving a multi-year custodial contract, and expanding free student breakfast pilots.

The committee governed operations through the COVID-19 pandemic, implementing distance learning models, pooled virus testing, and phased school reopening protocols while renaming the Columbus Elementary School to the Missituk School and approving a multi-year district strategic plan.
